notes:
Literally "sucking blood" — a compound of {吸|きゅう} (to suck/inhale) + {血|けつ} (blood). Used both for the literal biological act (mosquitoes, ticks, leeches) and in the context of vampire fiction.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {吸血|きゅうけつ}{鬼|き}: vampire (literally "blood-sucking demon")
- {吸血|きゅうけつ}コウモリ: vampire bat
- {吸血|きゅうけつ}⟦{行為|こうい}→行為：10021_koui⟧: act of blood-sucking
- {吸血|きゅうけつ}⟦{昆虫|こんちゅう}→昆虫：05010_konchuu⟧: blood-sucking insect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{吸血鬼|きゅうけつき}→吸血鬼：12011_kyuuketsuki⟧: vampire (the creature itself; most common compound)
- ⟦{採血|さいけつ}→採血：11074_saiketsu⟧: drawing blood (medical procedure; neutral/clinical term)
- ⟦{輸血|ゆけつ}→輸血：04083_yuketsu⟧: blood transfusion (medical procedure of transferring blood)

USAGE:
In everyday Japanese, {吸血|きゅうけつ} appears most often as a modifier in compounds like ⟦{吸血鬼|きゅうけつき}→吸血鬼：12011_kyuuketsuki⟧ (vampire). The verb form {吸血|きゅうけつ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ is used mainly in scientific or nature documentary contexts to describe how animals feed on blood.
